name: Ladder: Registration response
summary: The server's registration answer. RegistrationResponseMsg (wire 0x3, S2C, 88-byte record / 85-byte body) carries the server's version as one prefix-varint string and moves the client from WaitingForREPConnection (14) to WaitingForActorGameConnection (15). The client speaks first with a separate message (wire 0x13, RegistrationRequestV3Msg); its request body is NOT modelled in this card.
purpose: Answer the client's registration with the server's own version string. The client sends its build first, so a private server's job here is to ANSWER that request, not to open the conversation.

created_when: the client has opened the REP connection and is waiting to register
lifecycle.if_absent: the client stays in WaitingForREPConnection and never reaches the actor game connection

envelope: Record envelope (owned by javelin/frame.py, not a body field): measured 00 01 03, the typed envelope plus the prefix varint 0x03, a one-byte varint because the value is below 0x80. fields[] below use BODY offsets, so the first body byte is at 0x00 and the 88-byte record starts 3 bytes earlier.

fields.name: unresolved_u32
fields.note: f1, measured zero, 4 bytes. The atlas states the codec but names no consumer. Big-endian follows the repo rule for fixed-width wire integers; the endianness itself is not measured.

fields.name: unresolved_u64
fields.note: f2, measured 0x0b888d68706c415b (bytes 0b 88 8d 68 70 6c 41 5b). The atlas corrects the old read that split this into a u8 (0x0b) at record 0x07 plus 8 bytes at record 0x08: it is ONE u64 BE. Still unnamed.

fields.name: unresolved_block
fields.note: f3: a prefix-varint length (0x20 = 32) then 32 raw bytes. Fully redacted in the published dump, so the content is lost; the size is stated, so the shape is carried as prefixed_bytes. Could be one 32-byte id or two 16-byte ids.

fields.name: server_version
fields.note: f4: a prefix-varint length (0x23 = 35) then '[RETAIL].Javelin.1.365.6031.6006993'. The handler labels the slot 'Server version'. The atlas corrects the old read that took the 0x23 byte as the first content byte of a fixed_string(36): it is the length prefix.

fields.name: trailing_bool_0
fields.note: f5: first of the four trailing bool bytes. Measured 01.

fields.name: trailing_bool_1
fields.note: f5: second of the four trailing bool bytes. Measured 00.

fields.name: trailing_bool_2
fields.note: f5: third of the four trailing bool bytes. Measured 00.

fields.name: trailing_bool_3
fields.note: f5: fourth of the four trailing bool bytes. Measured 01. The four bytes 01 00 00 01 are the last four of the body; the atlas says four bool bytes, and only f4 is named.

evidence.ref: services/world/replay/messages-redacted.txt record 0x1_T0x3_R.bin: 88 bytes, seq 0x1, direction R, type 0x3. Offsets sum exactly: 3 header + 4 + 8 + 1 + 32 + 1 + 35 + 4 = 88

research/atlas/meanings.md 'flow.world-entry.rung.registration.body': the server->client half is wire 0x3 RegistrationResponseMsg, an 88-byte record, layout measured to the byte (writer 0x1407cd050 and reader 0x1407cd1e0 agree): f1 u32 BE; f2 u64 BE; f3 prefix-varint length + 32 raw bytes; f4 prefix-varint length + the 35-byte server_version; f5 four bool bytes. f4 is named; f1/f2/f3/f5 are codec-identified but unnamed

handler FUN_1464768a0, .pdata 0x1464768a0-0x146476a1d (381 bytes), vtable slot 0x148503e28, reached through the adjustor thunk 'add rcx,8; jmp' at 0x146476896. It logs 'GameConnectionWrapper: received registration response from REP', passes the message to a virtual setter labelled 'Server version' (slot +0x2d0), then reads the client's own version string through a getter and hands it to the setter at +0x110

two independent signals agree that this body carries a server version: the decompiled handler labels the setter 'Server version', and the captured 88-byte body literally contains a version string in the client's own format

third independent signal, added 2026-10-25 after the scan-wire-names.py fix: research/derived/wire-type-names.json now resolves slot 3 to RegistrationResponseMsg. That name was not available when the rung was identified, because the scanner had been unrunnable since private-client/ moved to the repo root

the version format is corroborated by reverse/builds/30fe6461.../corpus/meta.json, whose 'versions' field is ['[RETAIL].Javelin.1.460.6033.6024067'], the same #[RETAIL].Javelin.<version> shape with the client's own build numbers

record 0x0_T0x13_W.bin: 2,750 bytes, direction W, type 0x13, the client's RegistrationRequestV3Msg. Its keyed-string pattern `<u32 BE key><u8 len><bytes>` reproduces on five consecutive runs at 0x20, 0x29, 0x31, 0x37 and 0x43, and key 8 at 0x45 has length 0x5b = 91 starting '[RETAIL]'. That request is a DIFFERENT message and is not modelled in this card

research/derived/wire-type-names.json resolves slot 19 (0x13) to RegistrationRequestV3Msg, slot 2 to RegistrationRequestV2Msg, slot 1 to RegistrationRequestMsg and slot 3 to RegistrationResponseMsg, so the whole registration family is named on this build

the client does NOT require an exact version match: the capture's client reports 1.400.6031.6004151 through the request keys while the server's response says '#[RETAIL].Javelin.1.365.6031.6006993', a different minor and revision, and the client still advanced. A private server can therefore answer with its own version string rather than having to impersonate the official one
